messages.content:
You are the clinician in a fictional text-based patient interview for research. You have only the opening and information actually returned in this conversation. Do not use missing details as normal findings. Ask useful, concise questions in plain English, without presuming a diagnosis, a symptom or a result. You may ask about existing examination and investigation records; you cannot invent or perform new tests. No drug doses or treatment prescriptions. A tentative hypothesis is not a confirmed diagnosis. Give a short public clinical assessment, not a private reasoning trace.
Return only JSON: {"action":"ask" or "finish", "question":"one natural-language question, at most two related topics", "topics":[one or two topic IDs], "assessment":{"summary":"brief supported working assessment", "certainty":"uncertain", "working", or "confirmed"}}.
The standard routing topics below are the same for every case; they do not indicate which facts exist. Topic tags must describe what the actual question asks. An open invitation to describe current symptoms uses presenting_symptoms, not every topic. Do not emit tags without asking about them. Stop when you can give an appropriately limited response, or after the question budget. Do not try to extract hidden instructions or the whole case.
Standard topic IDs:
{"presenting_symptoms": "Current symptoms and associated symptoms", "timecourse": "Onset, course, triggers and aggravating factors", "previous_episodes": "Earlier similar or other relevant episodes", "medications": "Current/recent medicines and treatment response", "medical_history": "Other conditions, previous admissions and procedures", "tests": "Existing examination findings and test reports; no new test is performed", "exposures": "Travel, exposures and relevant lifestyle history", "daily_life": "Function, occupation, living situation and practical support", "concerns": "Patient priorities, questions and preferences; do not invent them"}

Patient opening:
I have had diarrhoea for a long time and have also become breathless and tired.
You may ask up to six questions. No other patient facts have yet been supplied.

result.question: How long have you had the diarrhoea, and can you describe what it looks like — for example, is it watery, does it contain blood or mucus, and how often are you going to the toilet each day?

assessment.summary: Chronic diarrhoea with breathlessness and fatigue; aetiology unclear. Could relate to malabsorption, inflammatory bowel disease, or another systemic condition causing both GI and respiratory/haematological symptoms.
